Ryukoku University Guide for 
Exchange Students 
Please read this guide VERY carefully before filling in the 
application form. We will explain and help you with your 
application preparation. As immigration procedures take a very 
long time for processing, please be sure to submit ALL required 
materials as early as possible.

2 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Please complete your application process while following the procedures below. 
 
Qualifications for Application 
Only students who are enrolled at universities which have a Student Exchange Agreement with Ryukoku University, 
and who have been nominated by their home university, are eligible to apply. 
 
Application Procedures 
The Home University Coordinator must complete the online form titled <2026 年度交換留学ノミネーシ
ョン／Fall 2026 Exchange Program Nomination Form>. 
Nomination Period: April 6th ~ April 30th, 2026 23:59 (Japan Time) 
 
The Nominated Students must receive a link from the Home University Coordinator for the online form titled 
<Exchange Application Fall 2026 Entry> and complete the form within the following period: 
Application Period: April 6th ~ May 13th, 2026 23:59 (Japan Time) 
 
① Notification of Acceptance or Non-Acceptance 
Those who have completed the above procedures by the deadline will be notified of their acceptance or non-
acceptance in approximately the middle of June. 
 
② Issuance of the Official Acceptance Letter and COE (Certificate of Eligibility) 
These documents will be sent to accepted students at approximately the beginning of August. 
 
 
 
 
 
To receive a student visa from the Japanese Embassy or Consulate, you need a Certificate of Eligibility (COE). The 
Ryukoku University Center for the Promotion of Global Education (R-Globe) Office will apply for this (in Japan) 
on your behalf, after we rece ive all your required application documents. It generally takes six to eight weeks for 
the Certificate to be issued, so be sure to submit all your materials as soon as possible to avoid any possible delay. 
Once we receive the Certificate of Eligibility, we  will send it together with the Letter of Acceptance to you in a 
“Welcome Package”, addressed to your home university. Once you receive these documents, please take the 
Certificate of Eligibility and the Letter of Acceptance to the Japanese Embassy in your own country to apply for 
your student visa. 
 
 
 
Certificate of Eligibility & Student Visa

Exchange students will primarily pursue their studies through the Ryukoku Japan Studies Program (JSP), which 
will be launched in April 2026. The JSP curriculum is built upon the university's guiding principle of "Magokoro" 
(sincerity, compassion, and altruism). It offers a combination of three subject groups: Japanese language study, 
international collaborative courses that involve Project-Based Learning (PBL) with domestic and other international 
students, and subjects focused on Japanese society, culture, and industry. 
 
In addition to courses offered in Japanese and elective subjects, JSP also offers many subjects taught in English. 
This allows a wide range of students to enroll, from Japanese  language beginners to advanced learners aiming to 
take the Japanese Language Proficiency Test (JLPT). This program is designed to provide significant academic and 
personal growth through field trips, cultural activities, and interaction with the local community.  Furthermore, 
students who meet certain conditions may also be permitted to enroll in courses offered by Ryukoku University’s  
undergraduate and graduate schools. Overall, during their exchange term, students are required to register for 15 or 
more credits per semester. 
 
 
 
 
 
●There are three courses of study for exchange students, as follows: 
① Ryukoku Japan Studies Program (JSP) 
This program aims to provide an opportunity for international students and local Ryukoku University students to 
learn together, deepen their understanding of different cultures and values, and develop practical communication 
skills. S tudents from diverse backgrounds collaborate in their classes through discussions, group work, and 
fieldwork. Subjects are offered in both Japanese and English. In addition, it is possible to complete the program 
entirely in English so students who have never studied Japanese are able to participate. 
If a student wishes to register for subjects conducted in Japanese, they must be assessed as having the necessary 
level of Japanese proficiency (based on the results of the Placement Test). If the student’s Japanese proficiency is 
not sufficient, they will take classes conducted in English.

About the Ryukoku University Japan Studies Program (JSP)

Furthermore, students assigned to classes JSP-1 ~ JSP-III may register for undergraduate-level and graduate-level 
subjects offered in English. Students assigned to classes  JSP-IV and JSP-V are eligible to register for all 
undergraduate-level and graduate-level subjects. 
② Registration for Regular Undergraduate Faculty Classes Only                                              
 
This option applies to Exchange Students who, based on the conditions set forth in the Student Exchange Agreement 
concluded between specific Faculties at both universities, may only register for classes in the Faculty to which they 
belong. (Ryukoku University Faculty of Economics and Dalian University of Foreign Languages School of Japanese 
Studies） 
 
③ Registration for Regular Graduate School Classes Only                                          
 
This option applies to Exchange Students who, based on the conditions set forth in a Student Exchange Agreement 
concluded between specific Graduate Schools at both universities, may only  register for classes in the Graduate 
School to which they belong. (Agreements concluded with our Graduate School of Advanced Science and 
Technology). 
 
 
 
 
●First, the student should confirm with the Study Abroad Coordinator at their home university regarding whether 
exchange student is possible under the existing Student Exchange Agreement. In some cases, due to agreements 
concluded between specific Faculties or Graduate Schools, the student may be limited to registering for subjects 
only within a specific major.  
● If the student selects the English Track, they will not be able to register for subjects conducted in Japanese. 
Careful consideration should be given to this choice, as the student will not be able to change their selection after 
applying. 
●For the Japanese track, it is recommended that the student has completed at least 300 hours of Japanese language 
study or has Japanese proficiency equivalent to JLPT N4 or higher.  
●Based on the results of the Japanese placement test, if the student’s Japanese level is determined to be lower than 
that required for entry into JSP-II, they may be reassigned to JSP-I (English Track) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The JSP curriculum is structured to include <Core Required Subjects> (for which credit acquisition is mandatory), 
<Required Enrollment Subjects> (which all students must take but credit acquisition is not mandatory), and 
<Elective Subjects>. Elective Subjects are divided into three clusters: Subject Cluster A ~ Subject Cluster C.

●You are required to register for a minimum of 15 credits per semester (30 credits per year). (Please note that this 
minimum registered credit requirement is subject to change.) Be sure to confirm with the responsible staff or 
faculty member at your home university regarding which fields of study you must complete studies in at 
Ryukoku University. 
● Students in JSP-IV and JSP-V may enroll in selected undergraduate and graduate school subjects in addition to 
their JSP subjects. Students in JSP I ~ III may only enroll in selected English-taught undergraduate and graduate 
courses outside of their JSP subjects. 
●You cannot enroll in certain subjects with enrollment restrictions, such as those that have a prerequisite system (先
修制) or are small-group classes like seminars (ゼミ) in the regular undergraduate and graduate programs. Prior 
permission to enroll is required for these courses.

Ryukoku University has three campuses in and around Kyoto. These campuses are close to train lines and within 
easy reach of each other, so you should be able to commute easily between them.  
*There are free shuttle buses between the campuses throughout the day, with Fukakusa as the central campus. (From 
Fukakusa to Omiya: 20 Minutes; From Fukakusa to Seta: 40 minutes).  
 
 
◆深 草 
FUKAKUSA Campus, located in southern Kyoto, is the central  campus.  
The Center for the Promotion of Global Education and all lectures in the JSP 
Program are based here. The Faculties of International Studies, Economics, 
Business Administration, Law, Policy Science, and Sociology, along with 
First and Second Year subjects of the Faculty of Letters and the Faculty of 
Psychology are located here. 
 
◆大 宮 
OMIY A Campus is our original campus (founded in 1639), and is located in 
central Kyoto, just beside historic Nishi Hongwanji Temple. Third and 
Fourth Year subjects of the Faculty of Letters and the Faculty of Psychology, 
as well as those of the Graduate School of Psychology, are taught here, and 
the campus provides an ideal calm and relaxed atmosphere for study and 
research. 
 
◆瀬 田 
SETA Campus, located in Shiga Prefecture’s “Biwako Culture Park”, is 
surrounded by nature and is the newest and largest campus, The Faculties of 
Advanced Science and Technology, Sociology and Agriculture are located 
here.

Rental Bedding is required for all dormitory residents. It is not possible to cancel this service.

The conditions of your exchange are based on the terms and conditions in the Student Exchange Agreement between 
your Home University and Ryukoku University. Please consult your Home University if you are unsure of these 
conditions. 
 
 
 
 
 
Financial transactions such as scholarship payments, dormitory fees, and electricity bills will, in principle, be 
handled through direct debit from a bank account. Therefore, a pre-arrival orientation is scheduled to be held around 
July, during which further details will be explained.  
 
Please note that it usually takes about two months after opening a bank account before automatic withdrawal for 
dormitory fees can be set up. Until then, payments must be made in cash at a convenience store. Credit cards and 
debit cards cannot be used.  
 
It is also advisable to open a bank account that can be used internationally (for example, CITIBANK, STAR, Cirrus, 
Maestro, etc.) before entering Japan. 
 
 
**IMPORTANT: Common Financial Problems After Arrival** 
 
 
It is always the case at the beginning of the semester that a few students have a very difficult time because they are 
not able to use the bank cards which they have brought with them from abroad and therefore are not able to withdraw 
the necessary funds for their everyday lives.  
① Please be sure to confirm with your card company/bank that: (1) you will immediately  be able to withdraw 
funds after arriving in Japan with your card, and (2) that you know exactly how to use the card. Please make it 
a point to remember your pin number to avoid having your account blocked. 
 
② It is sometimes the case that students do not inform the bank in their home country of their exchange study 
period, and their bank card is frozen due to sudden use in another country. Please be sure to inform your bank 
that you will be studying abroad to avoid this problem.  
 
③ There is often a daily limit for withdrawing money internationally from one’s bank in their home country. Please 
be well aware of what the daily limit is, so you can surely make initial dormitory payments, as well as have 
enough for initial living expenses. If your bank will not allow you to withdraw enough money shortly after your 
arrival, please be sure to bring sufficient funds with you. 
 
Exchange Conditions 
 
Bank Accounts

Regardless of whether you are insured in your home country, students who will study in Japan for more than three 
months (i.e., three months and one day or longer) are required to enroll in Japan’s National Health Insurance system. 
The insurance premium is approximately 1,500 to 2,000 yen per month. Enrollment procedures must be completed 
at the ward office near the university after admission.  
 
Before traveling to Japan, you must enroll in overseas travel insurance or accident insurance that covers the entire 
duration of your exchange program. In particular, choosing a plan that includes personal liability coverage can help 
reduce financial burdens in the event of unexpected accidents. 
 
To ensure a safe and secure study abroad experience, please make sure to enroll in appropriate insurance and review 
the coverage details prior to your departure.

Procedures for Dormitory Entry 
Ryukoku University International Student Dormitories 
General Rules

13 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
① After submitting the application form to enter the Ryukoku University International Student 
Dormitory, the Student Information Centre (NASIC) 【※】will send you an email for information 
regarding your arrival date, and provide a document about the date you will enter the dormitory. 
Decide your move-in date and return the completed documents to NASIC by the specified date by 
email. 
【※】[NASIC is the private company which manages the dormitories on behalf of the Center for the 
Promotion of Global Education (R-Globe) Office]. 
 
② Please sign the [Pledge] and return it to NASIC. 
 
③ Regarding your First Payment 
For those staying at [Mitra-kan], [Ryukoku International House]: 
Please make your payment of the Security Deposit and <First Time> Usage Fees [Rent, Utilities, Bedding 
(optional)] at the nearest convenience store shortly after your arrival. This payment must be made in cash. IT 
IS NOT POSSIBLE TO PAY BY CREDI T OR DEBIT CARD. Also, please note t hat Yucho Ginko 
(Japan Post Bank) does not offer online banking services. 
 
④ Security Deposit  
In principle, the security deposit will be returned when you check-out of the dormitory, by bank transfer on 
a specific day designated by NASIC. However, if you have failed to pay your room rent or utilities fees, or 
if payment is required for any damages caused to the room or dormitory, the required fees will be deducted 
from this security deposit. If the amount required exceeds the amount of the security deposit, a bill will be 
sent to you for the excess amount. Students with a room rental waiver are not required to pay a security 
deposit. 
 
⑤ Automatic Account Withdrawal 
Room rent and utilities fees will be automatically withdrawn from your bank account on a designated day 
of the month.  
If you do not have a bank account available in Japan when you enter the dormitory, you will open one. 
The account will be at Yucho Ginko. Please complete the form for opening an account and submit it by the 
specified date. 
<<Required Documents>> 
• Form for opening the bank account (to be distributed after you enter the dormitory) 
• Residence Card copy 
 
For those staying at [Mitra-kan], [Ryukoku International House]: 
Each month’s room rent and utilities expenses will be automatically withdrawn from your bank account on 
the 6th of each month (in the case that the 6 th is a weekend or national holiday, on the following business 
day). 
※Automatic withdrawal is possible from any Japanese bank. However, those who have not formerly 
opened a Japanese bank account will have an account established at Y ucho Ginko (Japan Post Bank) 
after their arrival in Japan. Please be sure to fill in this account on your automatic withdrawal form. 
 
⑥ Move-In Day 
  You will be given guidance by either a Resident Supporter【※】or the Dormitory Manager. 
  【※】The Resident Supporters are Japanese students of Ryukoku University who live in the dormitories 
to provide international students with assistance regarding their daily lives at the dorms and at the 
university in general. If you have any difficulties, please either consult either the Resident Supporters or 
the Center for the Promotion of Global Education (R-Globe) Office.

All dormitory residents (including students with a room rental waiver) are required to pay monthly utilities 
fees, even during break periods in between semesters. 
 
If a room is occupied for less than 15 days of any calendar month, rent will be calculated by the day. If the 
room is occupied from the 15th of the month on, the cost of one month will be charged. If you wish to prorate 
your rent for less than 15 days, you must submit a notice of withdrawal to the Dormitory Manager by the 5th 
of the month preceding the month in which you are leaving the dormitory. If you submit the notice after the 
due date, you will be charged one month's rent, even if you leave within 14 days. 
 
If a [SINGLE] room at Ryukoku International House is occupied for the first eight days of the month, he/she 
will be charged according to the following: 
 
(International Student: 1 month rent 45,000JPY <Room Rent: 35,000JPY , Utilities 10,000JPY> 
↓ 
(45,000 JPY ÷ 30 days ×8 days = 12,000 JPY [Final charge: 12,000 JPY] ） 
Calculation Method: Monthly Fee ÷30 (days) × Number of Days Occupied. All decimal points are cut. 
 
 
 
 
 
①Due to the great number of students arriving in March and August, Occupants checking out must depart by 
March 19 or August 10 (If this day falls on a weekend or public holiday, checkout must take place on the 
previous day). Rent and utilities fees will be calculated according to [Rules: Dorm Rent and Utilities] above. 
 
② Rental fees, once paid, will not be refunded except in special circumstances. Notification of leaving the 
dormitory must be submitted at least one month in advance. 
 
 
 
 
 
① Please be sure to submit a “Leaving the Dormitory” form to your Dormitory Manager by the 7 th of the 
month previous to the month you plan to depart. If you fail to turn in the form by that time, even if you 
plan to reside in your room for only 14 days or less in the following month, you will be charged the full 
rent amount. 
② Clean your room and remove your belongings before checking out. 
 
③ Approximately One Week before Checkout: Your Resident Supporter will conduct a room check. 
 
④  On Checkout Day: Your Resident Supporter will conduct a room check. This room check is required! 
⑤ Once your electricity fee has been calculated and the condition of your room checked, your Security 
Deposit will be refunded. 
■In the following cases, occupants will be required to leave the Dormitory: 
◎ Termination of studies at Ryukoku University 
◎ Expiration of contract 
◎ Rejection of application to extend one’s Period of Stay 
◎ Decision by the university that the occupant is no longer eligible to continue living in the dormitory

Checking Out Procedures

◎ Where delayed payment or compensation exceeds the rental deposit amount 
◎ Failure to obey dormitory rules 
◎ Deliberate disobedience of university guidelines and instructions 
◎ Failure to fulfill one’s obligations as a dormitory resident 
 
■Leaving the Dormitory During the Residence Term 
If you wish to leave the dormitory before the resident period expires, notification must be provided to NASIC 
*AT LEAST* one month in advance. 
*If you wish to reside in the dormitory with a daily rate (for less than 15 days), you must submit a [Leaving 
the Dormitory Notice] to the Dormitory Manager by the 5th of the PREVIOUS month you will check out of 
the dormitory. If this notice is submitted a fter the deadline, you will be charged the dormitory fee for the 
entire month (even if you depart within the first fourteen days of the month). 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Please observe the following regulations: 
 
①Dormitory property is not to be altered or misused in any way. 
②No economic or political activity may be carried out within the dormitory. 
③Dormitory furnishings or equipment are not to be removed. 
④Potential fire hazards such as gas ranges are not to be used outside designated areas 
⑤Occupants should follow dormitory rules and respect Japanese customs. 
⑥Do not disturb fellow residents or people living in the surrounding neighborhood. 
（e.g. making loud noise, leaving rubbish in the corridor/on the streets etc.） 
⑦Care should be taken to keep both one’s room and the communal living areas clean and sanitary. 
⑧Fires, thefts, etc. should be reported immediately 
 
●Cohabitation is prohibited. 
A single room may only have 1 occupant. 
 
●Entrance to other Residents’ rooms is prohibited. 
You may not enter the rooms of other Residents, even in the case of friends. 
 
●Overnight guests are not permitted. 
Family and friends are not allowed to stay overnight in the dormitory. They are required to leave the 
dormitory premises by the curfew designated by each dormitory. 
 
●Smoking 
Smoking is not allowed within dormitory premises belonging to Ryukoku University (even outside the 
building) 
 
●Overnight Trips 
If you go away for an extended period or return to your home country, you must contact the Center for 
the Promotion of Global Education Office at least 1 week in advance.  
Ryukoku International House ・Mitra-kan Residents: Fill out Out- of-Town Overnight Stay Form, 
available by QR Code. 
※Please note that it is not possible to check out of the  
dormitory on a Saturday, Sunday, or National Holiday. 
 
Mandatory Code of Conduct

16 
 
 
●Use of Parking Facilities 
Please put an identification sticker on your bicycle (These stickers can be attained from the Resident 
Supporters). Do not leave your bicycle at the dormitory after you move out. In the case of theft, please 
report it directly to the police (not the University). 
Ryukoku University will not be held responsible for any cases of theft. 
 
●Pets 
Pets are strictly forbidden in the dormitory.  
 
●Mailbox 
Affix your name to your dormitory mailbox and be sure to check it at least once a day. 
●Regarding Dormitory Fee Delinquency 
If the dormitory fee payment is overdue for two consecutive months, you will be required to leave the 
dormitory. Please make sure to pay the fee by the due date. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
In addition to the rules above, each dormitory has 
its own regulations. If you fail to follow the 
regulations, you will be asked to leave the 
dormitory.
